label: AI Agents & Tools
title: AI Agents and Tool Use
body:
An AI agent is an LLM that can do more than just chat — it can take actions in the real world. While a standard chatbot only generates text, an agent can search the web, send emails, query databases, or run code. The secret? Tool calling (also called function calling): the model outputs a structured request saying which tool to use and what parameters to pass, then external code actually runs that tool and feeds the result back.

The classic pattern is ReAct (Reasoning + Acting): the model alternates between thinking through a problem and taking actions to gather information, looping until it reaches an answer. This lets agents tackle multi-step tasks that require real-time data or interaction with other systems.

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) — introduced by Anthropic in 2024 and now adopted by OpenAI and Google — standardises how agents connect to tools. Think of it like USB-C for AI: one universal interface instead of custom code for every integration. This makes building agents with dozens or hundreds of tools far more practical.
